title: 第一卷 第8章 夜访寡妇家门
slug: 满门遗孀花甲老汉粮肉满仓
content_zh:
第(1/3)页

林骁循着野猪脚印，在深山里走了一个多时辰。

雪地难行，但林骁却始终没有放弃。

终于，在一处背风的山坳里，他看见了那个大家伙。

一头棕黑色的野猪，正用长嘴拱开积雪，翻找草根和橡果。

它肩背高耸，獠牙外露，目测不下二百斤，浑身鬃毛在雪光下泛着油亮。

林骁屏息，缓缓搭箭。

野猪浑然不觉，仍在埋头觅食。

弓弦拉满，指尖一松。

“嗖——”

箭矢破空，精准扎进野猪脖颈与肩胛的衔接处。

那是野猪的要害，皮薄，血管密集。

“嗷——！”

野猪发出一声凄厉嘶吼，猛地人立起来，又重重落地。

它转头，血红的小眼睛死死盯向林骁的方向，随即撒开四蹄，朝密林深处狂奔。

林骁不慌不忙，收起弓，循着雪地上的血迹追去。

血迹断断续续，洒在雪上格外刺目。

追了约莫半个时辰，在一处枯木堆旁，他再次见到了那野猪。

它已力竭，侧躺在地上，腹部剧烈起伏，脖颈处的箭杆随着呼吸微微颤抖。

但那双眼睛仍瞪得滚圆，充满凶光。

林骁在十步外站定，再次搭箭。

“嗖！嗖！嗖！”

三箭连发，分别钉入咽喉、心口、眼窝。

野猪最后抽搐几下，终于不动了。

林骁这才上前，踢了踢猪身，确认死透。

他拔出箭矢，在雪地上擦净血迹，收回箭囊。

这头野猪，少说二百斤。

省着吃，够一家四口撑过这个冬天。

若拿去卖，能换不少银钱。

但怎么弄下山，是个问题。

日头已到中天。

林骁找了块石头坐下，从怀里掏出干粮，啃了起来。

吃完，体力恢复些许，他起身，将野猪四蹄捆紧，找了根粗木穿过，扛上肩。

他咬紧牙，一步步往山下挪。

终究是上了年纪，走一段就得歇一会儿。

等到村口时，已是黄昏。

几个村民正在井边打水，见他扛着这么大一头野猪，全都瞪直了眼。

“我的娘……老林头打的？”

“这寒冬腊月的，还能猎到野猪？”

“还是这么大一头……”

有人凑上前，满脸堆笑：“林老哥，好本事啊！这猪……分点儿？”

林骁停下脚步，喘匀了气，笑道：“想要肉？行啊，拿钱来换。”

Page (1/3)

Lin Xiao followed the wild boar's footprints and walked in the mountains for more than an hour.

It was difficult to walk in the snow, but Lin Xiao never gave up.

Finally, in a leeward mountain col, he saw the big guy.

A brown-black wild boar was digging through the snow with its long beak, looking for grass roots and acorns.

It had tall shoulders and back, exposed fangs, weighed no more than two hundred pounds, and its mane was shiny under the snowy light.

Lin Xiao held his breath and slowly nocked the arrow.

The wild boar was unaware and was still looking for food.

The bowstring is fully drawn, and the fingertips are loosened.

"Whoosh——"

The arrow broke through the air and accurately penetrated the connection between the wild boar's neck and shoulder blade.

That is the vital part of a wild boar, with thin skin and dense blood vessels.

"Ouch——!"

The wild boar let out a shrill roar, stood up abruptly, and then fell heavily to the ground.

It turned its head, its small blood-red eyes stared in Lin Xiao's direction, then spread its hooves and ran wildly deep into the dense forest.

Lin Xiao didn't panic, put away his bow, and chased after the blood stains on the snow.

The blood was intermittent, and it was particularly dazzling when sprinkled on the snow.

After chasing for about half an hour, he saw the wild boar again beside a pile of dead wood.

It was exhausted, lying on its side on the ground, its abdomen heaving violently, and the arrow shaft at its neck trembled slightly with its breathing.

But those eyes were still round and full of fierceness.

Lin Xiao stood ten steps away and cocked his arrow again.

"Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!"

Three arrows were fired in succession, piercing the throat, heart, and eye sockets respectively.

The wild boar twitched a few times and finally stopped moving.

Lin Xiao then stepped forward and kicked the pig's body to confirm that it was dead.

He pulled out the arrow, wiped the blood on the snow, and put back the quiver.

This wild boar weighs at least two hundred pounds.

If you save money, it will be enough for a family of four to survive this winter.

If you sell it, you can get a lot of money.

But how to get down the mountain is a problem.

The sun has reached its zenith.

Lin Xiao found a stone and sat down, took out the dry food from his arms and started to eat it.

After eating and regaining some strength, he stood up, tied the wild boar's hooves tightly, found a thick log to pass through, and carried it on his shoulders.

He gritted his teeth and moved down the mountain step by step.

After all, I am getting older, so I have to take a break after walking for a while.

By the time we arrived at the entrance of the village, it was already dusk.

Several villagers were fetching water from the well, and they all stared blankly when they saw him carrying such a big wild boar.

"My mother... was beaten by Lao Lintou?"

"Can we still hunt wild boars in this cold winter?"

"It's still so big..."

Someone came forward with a smile on his face: "Brother Lin, what a skill! This pig...does it matter?"

Lin Xiao stopped, took a breath, and said with a smile: "Want meat? Okay, I'll give you money in exchange."
